next_steps.action: Locate the shorted component before re-applying any power. Use a current-limited bench supply at the rail's nominal voltage set to a low current limit (0.5 A), then thermal camera or freeze spray / finger to find the hot component.

measure.what: Voltage drop / temperature across candidate components
measure.where: Output inductor, low-side MOSFET, output bulk capacitors, load ICs on the rail
measure.instrument: Bench supply with current limit + thermal camera or freeze spray
measure.expected: Shorted component heats up rapidly; healthy components stay cool.
measure.safety: Current-limit the bench supply at 0.5 A or less to avoid burning a trace. Do NOT use the laptop's own adapter.

interpretations.then: Low-side MOSFET likely shorted drain-to-source. Remove and re-measure the rail resistance. Replace only with a verified-compatible part (see ReplacementMappings).
Shorted output capacitor. Replace with same value/voltage/temp rating.
Short inside the load IC (e.g. PCH, memory, GPU). Likely board-level write-off unless the IC can be replaced.
Short is in a high-impedance path. Increase current limit gradually and re-scan, or use a milliohm meter to localise by trace drop.
